When a service is necessary, the system checks if your car is still registered.
If it is registered, you are notified.
If you do not go to the service, you are fined after 30 days.
At the car service facility the mechanic enters the problems of your car for reference.
While you wait (can take several days), you get status updates via email.
You can pay through the app, when the repair is done.
The mechanic enters that the repair was successful and you got your "Pickerl".
The mechanic enters the time for you next service.

result.process_description:
Title: Car Service

The police has a new app to remind you of your car service.
The process is started after a successful service.
When a service is necessary, the system checks if your car is still registered.
If it is registered, you are notified.
If you do not go to the service, you are fined after 30 days.
At the car service facility the mechanic enters the problems of your car for reference.
While you wait (can take several days), you get status updates via email.
You can pay through the app, when the repair is done.
The mechanic enters that the repair was successful and you got your "Pickerl".
The mechanic enters the time for you next service.

result.rule: Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Use bpmn:sendTask or bpmn:receiveTask when sending or waiting for a message is itself the modeled unit of work.

Respect event positions: a none intermediate event is catch-only in normal flow and never on a boundary; link events are intermediate-only, thrown and caught in pairs at the same process level, and a catching link has no incoming sequence flow; terminate is an end event only.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
A white-box participant references its process with processRef. A black-box participant has no processRef and no modeled internal workflow.
Use an intermediate catch event when flow waits for a trigger and an intermediate throw event when flow emits or raises a result.

result.rule: When the description says that a participant is given a physical item or device for use before a later notification: Model receiving the item as an activity, and model waiting for the later notification as an intermediate catch event before the described follow-up activity.

When the description says that a participant performs an action to confirm or verify that an outcome occurred: Model the confirmation as an activity; use a catch event only when the description says the process waits for a message, signal, time, or condition.

When the description says to send work to another participant and request changes until an acceptance condition is met, without describing distinct incoming messages for each iteration: Model one response-receiving activity or message-catching event before the acceptance decision, and loop the exchange through that decision; do not add separate receiving elements for inferred intermediate responses.

When the description says an order is placed and separately says that processing must finish before the flow continues: Model placing the order as an activity, then model waiting for processing to finish as an intermediate catch event, not as a receive task.
